title: Delhi Speaker Vijender Gupta Meets Indian Diaspora in Lima, Pushes Business and Cultural Ties
excerpt: During his Peru visit, Gupta praised the diaspora as ambassadors of Indian culture and held talks on expanding Indian business presence in Peru and neighbouring markets.
body:
• Delhi Legislative Assembly Speaker Vijender Gupta met members of the Indian community in Lima, Peru, during his visit to the country last month, an official statement said.
  • Gupta praised the diaspora's contributions to business, enterprise and cultural outreach, calling overseas Indians ambassadors of India's culture, traditions and heritage.
  • The interaction included a substantive exchange on expanding the presence of Indian businesses in Peru and neighbouring markets.
  • The Lima visit followed Gupta's September 23 study tour to Brazil, where he called on Rio de Janeiro's acting governor to deepen institutional cooperation.

Delhi Legislative Assembly Speaker Vijender Gupta held a warm interaction with members of the Indian community in Lima, Peru, praising the diaspora's role in business, enterprise and cultural outreach in the South American nation, according to an official statement issued in New Delhi on September 28.

The Lima meeting

The engagement, reported by IANS, brought into focus the growing contribution of the Indian diaspora in Peru and its role in strengthening India's presence in the wider region. Gupta spoke with community members about their professional and entrepreneurial journeys and praised their achievements across different fields, the statement said.

He noted that Indians living abroad serve not only as economic contributors but also as important ambassadors of India's culture, traditions and heritage, helping deepen people-to-people ties between India and Peru. The interaction also saw a substantive exchange on opportunities to expand the presence of Indian businesses in Peru and neighbouring markets, with community members sharing their views and suggestions on strengthening commercial engagement.

Context: India's Latin America push

The visit fits a broader pattern of Indian parliamentary diplomacy in Latin America. On September 23, Gupta called on the acting governor of the Brazilian state of Rio de Janeiro, appellate judge Ricardo Couto de Castro, during a study tour to Brazil — pushing for deeper institutional cooperation and knowledge exchange between India and Brazil. That meeting took place at the presidency of the Court of Justice of Rio de Janeiro, where the two dignitaries exchanged views on democratic governance, public institutions and mutual interests, according to the Delhi Legislative Assembly Secretariat.

India has been steadily widening its engagement with Latin America in recent years — from pharmaceuticals and IT services to agriculture and energy — and the Indian diaspora, though smaller there than in North America or the Gulf, plays an outsized role as a commercial and cultural bridge.

Diaspora angle

For the Indian community in Peru — entrepreneurs, professionals and families far from the spotlight that falls on diaspora gatherings in the US or UAE — a visit from a presiding officer of an Indian legislature is a recognition that their role matters to New Delhi. Gupta underlined the importance of sustained diaspora participation in building stronger economic linkages and widening India's institutional, business and cultural engagement in Latin America.

What's next

The statement gave no concrete deals, but the direction is clear: converting diaspora goodwill into commercial footprint. Whether Indian businesses expand in Peru and its neighbours will depend less on speeches and more on follow-through — trade missions, regulatory facilitation and the entrepreneurs Gupta met in Lima actually doing business back home.
